To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the methodology of strategic intelligence analysis is not a substitute but a complementary tool to the human agent.

(1) the methodology is based on a combination of human evaluation and computational analysis; (2) the methodology is not a replacement for human meaning-making but provides a tool for human agents to better understand the "Big picture" from textual data; (3) the methodology can be applied to any domain where meaning extraction from textual data is relevant.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions: (a) What is meaning-making?
the following questions: How can we make sense of large amounts of data?
the development of an intelligent system for strategic intelligence that combines computational processing of textual information with human evaluation and meaning-making.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
strategic intelligence involves the efforts of the human agent to understand the "big picture" emerging from data, which is a process of information processing and meaning-making.
this methodology provides a tool for the identification of the "Big Picture".
the methodology presented in this paper is an effective and efficient method for the extraction of meaning and the identification of emerging patterns of meaning from textual data.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the proposed methodology can be seen as an attempt to bridge the gap between information processing and meaning-making.
the proposed methodology can be seen as a new approach to the analysis of news articles.
it is a new methodology that can provide a new perspective on the process of strategic intelligence analysis.
The main takeaway from our work is that
meaning extraction from text is not an isolated process but is part of a larger process of strategic intelligence analysis.
the construction of maps from textual data can provide a new approach for strategic analysis of intelligence.
meaning extraction can benefit from the combination of computational and cognitive approaches to information processing.
